Antecedentes Clínicos:
Tendinopatía rotuliana bilateral.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones en significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones.
Condropatía superficial la faceta medial y vértice de la rótula.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Engrosamiento y aumento de señal del tercio proximal y medio del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de
rotura.
Aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital, sin signos de rotura.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales. No hay
alteraciones de señal de la grasa de Hoffa.
Impresión:
Condropatía superficial de la faceta medial y vértice de la rótula.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal y media. Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal.

Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Transformación quística parcial del LCA. LCP y ligamentos colaterales dentro de límites normales.
El menisco medial es de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Menisco lateral de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios que sugieran una rotura evidente.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Leve
displasia troclear.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de distribución difusa de la rótula, sin cambios óseos
secundarios. Aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
Leve aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital. No hay signos de rotura.
Tendón rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites
normales. Discreto edema de las partes blandas entre la banda de tibial y el cóndilo femoral
lateral.
Impresión:
Condropatía rotuliana con lesiones grado 2 y 3.
Leve displasia troclear.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital distal.
Probables signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de la rótula y de fricción de la banda
iliotibial, correlacionar con clínica

Technique: MRI of the knee. MCL normal. ACL normal. Edema of suprapatelar fat pat. Medial meniscus degenerative changes grade 2. Lateral meniscus normal. Cartilage normal. No joint effusion or cysts are present. Conclusion: Medial meniscus degenerative changes grade 2.

FINDINGS:

Prominent bone contusions in the medial aspect of the medial femoral condyle, lateral tibial plateau, posterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau, proximal metaphyseal region of the tibia, fibular head and anteroinferior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. Suspected microtrabecular impaction fracture at the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau.

Fluid:
Moderate joint effusion. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Normal.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Normal.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Complete full-thickness tear at the proximal third of the anterior cruciate ligament, the tibial insertion is unremarkable. The posterior cruciate ligament is normal.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Mild signal abnormality at the medial facet of the patella without full-thickness chondral fissures or subchondral reactive changes.
The extensor mechanism is unremarkable.
Small amount of fluid in the topography of the infrapatellar ligament.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Edema of the popliteus muscle, likely traumatic in nature/sprain.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:

1.Prominent bone contusions at the medial femoral condyle, lateral tibial plateau, posterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau, proximal metaphyseal region of the tibia, fibular head and anteroinferior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. Suspected microtrabecular impaction fracture at the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau. Moderate joint effusion.
2.Complete full-thickness tear at the proximal third of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain post basketball injury.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 3 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Osteochondral impaction injury with accompanying bone marrow edema along the sulcus terminalis of the lateral femoral condyle with additional small osseous contusions along the posterior medial and lateral tibial plateaus. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No ossified intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal full thickness cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Osteochondral impaction injury along the lateral femoral condyle; otherwise, no focal full-thickness cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal full-thickness cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete midsubstance rupture.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Intact

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intrasubstance and periligamentous edema consistent with grade 2 sprain.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Intact; mild periligamentous edema along the fibular collateral ligament consistent with grade 1 sprain with additional mild periligamentous and intrasubstance edema involving the proximal popliteus tendon consistent with grade 2 sprain.
Posterolateral corner structures: Grade 1 sprain of the fibular collateral ligament with additional grade 2 sprain of the proximal popliteus tendon. Additional grade 1-2 sprain of the popliteal fibular ligament.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No high-grade tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No high-grade tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Mild periligamentous edema at its femoral attachment likely related to the adjacent MCL injury.
Patellofemoral tracking: No suspicious edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Minor lateral patellar tilt without significant translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy.   

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Mild subcutaneous and deep soft tissue edema on a posttraumatic basis.

IMPRESSION:
1. Complete midsubstance ACL rupture. Accompanying osteochondral impaction injury along the lateral femoral condyle and small osseous contusions along the posterior medial and lateral tibial plateaus.
2. Intact medial and lateral menisci.
3. Grade 2 MCL sprain.

Síndrome meniscal medial.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.

Condropatía focal grado 4 del aspecto inferior de la vertiente medial de la tróclea femoral.

Tendinosis cuadricipital distal y rotuliana proximal.
Probables fenómenos de fricción de la banda iliotibial

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain since [DATE]
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with a dominant oblique undersurface component and mild extrusion of the body.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Mild chondrosis with low-grade partial cartilage loss of the lateral patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 17 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Medial gastrocnemius origin tendinosis.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

1.	Complex tear of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with mild extrusion.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WITHOUT CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE]
Indication: Chronic knee pain. Associated locking, buckling, giving out, and popping/clicking. Associated intermittent swelling.
Comparison: Left knee radiographs [DATE], left knee MRI [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Patchy signal in the distal femoral metadiaphyseal region is favored to represent hematopoetic reconversion. Mild tricompartmental marginal spurring.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is a full-thickness fissuring with subchondral edema along the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle. Low-grade partial-thickness fissuring along the central medial tibial plateau. [REDACTED].

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness chondral loss along the lateral femoral condyle toward the intercondylar notch anteriorly. [REDACTED]. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness chondrosis at the lateral patellar facet, lateral, and central trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: Mild insertional tendinosis at the tibial tuberosity on a background of enthesopathy.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Minimal lateral patellar tilt and translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	[REDACTED].
2.	Mild distal quadriceps and distal patellar tendinosis. No tear.

Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colateral lateral sin alteraciones.
Engrosamiento de predominio baja señal del componente superficial del ligamento colateral
medial con mínimo edema. Aumento de señal con pérdida parcial continuidad el componente
profundo menisco femoral del complejo medial. El resto de los componentes del complejo medial
sin alteraciones.
Rotura compleja con componente principal horizontal oblicuo del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del
menisco medial con edema las partes blandas adyacentes. Edema óseo periférico del platillo tibial
medial de manera reactiva. No hay significativo desplazamiento de segmentos.
El menisco lateral es de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura. Cartílagos de los

Mínimo derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Engrosamiento y aumento de señal con probable pequeña rotura intrasustancia de la región distal
del tendón rotuliano. Tendón cuadricipital con aumento de señal. Engrosamiento con discreto
edema de la aponeurosis prepatelar.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.

Signos de un esguince grado II, probablemente en etapa subaguda del componente superficial y
profundo del complejo ligamentario medial.
Rotura compleja del menisco medial con edema las partes blandas regionales y edema óseo
periférico del platillo tibial medial de manera reactiva.
Condropatía lesiones grado 4 de la tróclea femoral.
Mínimo derrame articular.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana distal con pequeña rotura intrasustancia.
Tendinosis cuadricipital distal. Engrosamiento y aumento de señal de la aponeurosis continua
prepatelar
